requirements.requirement: Pin/hold curl at its currently installed version (8.17.0-r1) on node1 so it is not upgraded by an apk update
requirements.summary: Executor identified installed curl 8.17.0-r1, confirmed an upgrade candidate (8.22.0-r0) existed, then edited /etc/apk/world to constrain curl=8.17.0-r1, which is the standard apk mechanism for holding a package version.

requirements.requirement: A real system update (apk upgrade) must leave curl untouched while other packages update normally
requirements.summary: apk upgrade --simulate no longer listed curl/libcurl after the pin, and a real apk upgrade of 133 packages was executed, upgrading unrelated packages (util-linux, pcre2, etc.) while curl/libcurl remained at 8.17.0-r1, confirmed via apk info/list and curl --version afterward.

requirements.requirement: The version hold should remain effective and curl should stay functional across a system restart
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id (f27bb0ed...) was captured, node1 was natively rebooted, and a new boot_id (7ba884c4...) confirmed the restart. Post-restart, curl-8.17.0-r1/libcurl-8.17.0-r1 remained installed, the world-file pin persisted, curl performed a successful HTTPS request, and a fresh apk update + upgrade --simulate still excluded curl, directly demonstrating the hold survives a reboot and re-synced index.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied the task: curl 8.17.0-r1 was pinned via /etc/apk/world, verified to survive both a simulated and a real 133-package apk upgrade, and confirmed to persist through a full node reboot with a changed boot identity, remaining pinned and functional afterward. Minor unreverted artifacts (/etc/apk/world.bak, /tmp/reboot.log) are low-risk residue.
limitations: The /etc/apk/world.bak backup file's final disposition was not directly captured by any snapshot (only /tmp contents were tracked in the fixed lifecycle observations), so it is unconfirmed whether it was cleaned up.

No package-health/failed-services differential specific to /etc/apk was captured beyond the fixed 'package-health' observation, which is unchanged before/after and does not itself confirm the pin state.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trace shows a coherent, minimal set of state-changing actions: backing up and editing /etc/apk/world (cmd-f383a21bb2d34277, backup retained as /etc/apk/world.bak but not confirmed cleaned up — minor residue not captured in final /etc scan), running a real full apk upgrade (cmd-f9cb873c9fb24f97) which was directly relevant to proving the hold survives a genuine 'system update' as the task specifies, and the mandated native reboot (cmd-dd419b697db14691) leaving a small /tmp/reboot.log artifact visible in the after-executor snapshot. No destructive, unbounded, or security-weakening mutations were observed; all mutations map to either satisfying the pin requirement or the restart evidence protocol. The unremoved /etc/apk/world.bak and /tmp/reboot.log are low-risk leftover artifacts.
